It has already long been known that what drives global weather patterns is the jet stream.

The atmosphere is in a constant state of trying to reach equilibrium due to large areas of temperature differences on land, sea, and the air.

Temperature differences are what cause pressure differences. In physics, pressure always tries to reach an equilibrium of constant pressue. In turn, pressure differences in an atmosphere of air create wind as high pressue tries to flow to areas of lower pressure and low pressure tries to go to higher pressure in an attempt to level out the pressure.

Except this can never fully happen on Earth due to the constant heat from the sun, vast oceans of water being a better conductor for heat than air, the rotation of the earth, and, of course, the resultant coriolis effect.
